The Meridian Review round closes 1 March 2026; every decision uses the rules as they stand on that date.  

R1 – Length: a manuscript must be at least 22 pages; exactly 22 satisfies this rule.  

R2 – Format: a manuscript must either use the official template or include documented revision history covering at least 3 years.  

R3 – Venue overlap: a manuscript presented at a Tier‑1 venue is not handled unless the presentation occurred **more than** 18 months before the deadline; exactly 18 months does not qualify.  

R4 – Prior rounds: a manuscript accepted in an earlier Meridian round is not handled if fewer than 5 years have elapsed since that round; exactly 5 years elapsed is acceptable.  

R5 – Paired submissions: permitted for **exactly** 2 manuscripts; 3 or more are not allowed. Both must independently satisfy R1 and R2. At least one of the two must satisfy R3; the other need not.  

R6 – Track D: a submission to Track D is exempt from R2, but in place of R2 it must carry **exactly** 2 endorsements; 1 endorsement is insufficient. The exemption applies only to R2 and no other rule.  

R7 – Retraction: any manuscript with an open retraction notice is not handled, overriding every other rule, including R9.  

R8 – Figures: the figure count must be between 8 and 45 inclusive. For a paired submission the maximum rises to 70 while the minimum remains 8.  

R9 – Figure adjustment: if a submission fails R8 **only** by having fewer than the minimum, it is padded up to the minimum and its verdict is PADDED; if it exceeds the applicable maximum, it is RETURNED outright.  

R10 – Withdrawals: a withdrawal in a prior round does not count as an acceptance for R4. A withdrawal also resets the R3 venue clock, treating the presentation date as the withdrawal date rather than the original date.  

Verdicts: **HANDLED** means all applicable rules are satisfied; **RETURNED** means at least one applicable rule is violated; **PADDED** applies only in the R9 case where padding fixes a short‑figure count and no other rule is broken—if another rule also fails, the verdict is RETURNED.
messages.A1:
The Meridian Review handling system evaluates every submission on the basis of ten numbered rules (R1‑R10) as they stand on the deadline 1 March 2026; the outcome is a single verdict: **HANDLED**, **RETURNED** or, in one narrow case, **PADDED**.

**R1 – Length.** A manuscript must contain at least 22 pages; exactly 22 pages meets the requirement.

**R2 – Format.** The submission must either use the official template *or* provide documented revision history covering three or more years.

**R3 – Venue overlap.** If the work was presented at a Tier‑1 venue, that presentation must have occurred **more than** 18 months before the deadline; an exactly‑18‑month gap does not satisfy R3.

**R4 – Prior rounds.** A manuscript that was accepted in a previous Meridian round is disqualified unless at least five full years have passed since that acceptance; exactly five years elapsed is acceptable.

**R5 – Paired submissions.** Only a pair of two manuscripts may be submitted together; three or more constitute an invalid form. Both members of the pair must independently satisfy R1 and R2, and **at least one** of them must also satisfy R3 (the other need not).

**R6 – Track D.** Submissions to Track D are exempt from R2, but in place of that rule they must carry exactly two endorsements; a single endorsement is insufficient. The exemption applies only to R2 and no other rule.

**R7 – Retraction.** Any manuscript bearing an open retraction notice is rejected outright, regardless of every other rule—including R9.

**R8 – Figures.** The figure count must lie between 8 and 45 inclusive. For a paired submission the upper bound expands to 70 figures while the lower bound remains 8.

**R9 – Figure adjustment.** If a manuscript fails R8 **only** by having fewer than the minimum, it is padded up to the required minimum and receives the verdict **PADDED** instead of RETURNED. Any excess over the applicable maximum triggers an immediate RETURNED verdict.

**R10 – Withdrawals.** A withdrawal in a prior round does not count as an acceptance for R4. However, a withdrawal resets the R3 clock: the presentation date is treated as the withdrawal date rather than its original date.

**Verdicts.**  
- **HANDLED** means the submission satisfies every rule that applies to it.  
- **RETURNED** means it fails at least one applicable rule (including an excess‑figure case under R9).  
- **PADDED** is used only for the specific R9 situation where the only deficiency is a sub‑minimum figure count and no other rule is violated; if any additional rule is broken, the verdict is RETURNED.

A manuscript must be at least 22 pages; exactly 22 pages meets the length requirement (R1).  

For format (R2) it is acceptable if **either** the official template is used **or** there exists documented revision history covering a continuous period of three years or more; satisfying only one of these two ways suffices.  

If the work was presented at a Tier‑1 venue, the presentation date must be *more than* 18 months before the 1 March 2026 deadline; a presentation exactly 18 months prior fails (R3).  

An earlier acceptance in any Meridian round disqualifies the submission unless at least five full years have elapsed since that round; exactly five years is acceptable (R4). A withdrawal in the previous round does not count as an acceptance for R4, and it resets the venue‑clock of R3 to the withdrawal date (R10).  

A paired submission consists of **exactly** two manuscripts. Each manuscript in the pair must independently satisfy both R1 and R2. At least one member of the pair must also satisfy R3; the other may fail R3 without invalidating the pair (R5). No three‑manuscript “pair” is permitted.  

Submissions to Track D are exempt from R2, but they must carry **exactly** two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient and does not waive any other rule (R6).  

If an open retraction notice exists for the manuscript, it is **RETURNED** outright, overriding every other provision, including the figure‑adjustment clause (R7).  

Figure counts: a single submission must contain between 8 and 45 figures inclusive. A paired submission may have up to 70 figures, but the minimum of 8 still applies (R8).  

If a manuscript fails R8 **only** by having fewer than 8 figures, it is padded up to 8 and its verdict is **PADDED**; any other failure together with an under‑figure count results in **RETURNED**. Exceeding the maximum (45 for single, 70 for paired) triggers an immediate **RETURNED**, regardless of other compliance (R9).  

The final decision follows this hierarchy: first apply R7 (retraction); next evaluate length, format, venue timing, prior‑round age, pairing rules, Track D endorsements, and figure limits; only when a submission fails solely the lower‑figure condition does R9 produce PADDED. All other failures yield RETURNED; satisfying every applicable rule yields HANDLED.
